families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer hosts combined with retained acid or DES-like polar phases to preserve hydrogen-bonded proton pathways in the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or bound polar liquid motifs support low-temperature continuity.
D3: biopolymer/plasticiser blending is an analogous route to suppress brittle disconnection below freezing.
D4: phosphoric-acid or DES speciation is supported as a non-crystallising proton source.
D6: starch/chitosan/PVA supply dense donor-acceptor hydrogen-bond networks.
D7: chitosan and low-level PA strategies support conducting-phase retention.

families.family_description: One-dimensional clay or tubular hosts are used to confine acid-rich conducting domains and improve pathway connectivity and retention.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric acid and acid-complex environments are supported as mobile proton sources under confinement.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite explicitly provide interconnected nanoconfinement.
D6: confined phosphoric acid supplies proton-relay functionality.
D7: clay hosts reduce leaching and retain the conducting phase.

families.family_description: Amorphous proton-conducting inorganic networks combined with hydrogen-bonding soft phases offer phase-stable transport and strong confinement.
descriptor_match: D1: phosphate glass is directly supported as an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D3: adding soft hydrogen-bonding phases is an analogous route to offset brittle low-temperature response.
D6: phosphate networks and OH-rich polymers provide dense proton-relay landscapes.
D7: phosphate glass offers strong immobilisation, though humidity sensitivity remains a caution.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan film plasticised with a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep-eutectic phase to retain a mobile hydrogen-bonded proton medium at low temperature.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-fluid continuity from DES-like polar phase
retention: chitosan matrix may hold high water/acid content without disintegration
transport_mode: mixed vehicular and H-bond relay through amine/OH and phosphate contacts
risk_flags: exact low-temperature conductivity not directly shown for this exact composition
excess acid loading may still increase leaching risk

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is reported to retain a highly hydrated/plasticised conducting phase without structural failure.
Choline chloride is supported as the complexing partner in a ChCl/PA deep eutectic proton-carrier environment.
Phosphoric acid is supported as a confined or complexed proton source rather than a neat crystallising phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: The claim pool supports chitosan with DES and separately supports ChCl/PA DES chemistry, but not this exact merged formulation. It is novel because it combines a retention-capable biopolymer scaffold with a specifically phosphoric deep-eutectic acid phase for the 182–299 K window.

instances.composition_description: A starch/PVA blended film using attapulgite as a 1-D nanoconfining filler and phosphoric acid as the retained proton-conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: bound-water and OH-rich blend may preserve continuity better than neat water domains
nanoconfinement: 1-D clay can guide interconnected acid-rich channels
mechanics: PVA/starch blending may reduce brittle channel loss versus a single rigid host
risk_flags: phosphoric-acid leaching remains possible at high loading
cold performance is inferred by analogy rather than directly measured

element_evidence.reason: Starch is supported as an OH-rich channel-forming and hydrogen-bond-dense host.
PVA contributes additional OH-mediated hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor density and blend compatibility.
Attapulgite is directly supported as a 1-D host that guides nanoconfined transport and helps retain acid.
Phosphoric acid is supported as the proton-conducting medium, with low-doping retention-focused use reported in starch systems.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy motif: biopolymer host plus film former plus 1-D clay plus phosphoric acid. The evidence pool supports each element separately, but not their exact combination, making it a targeted novel assembly.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane loaded with halloysite nanotubes prehosting phosphoric acid to create retained tubular proton pathways.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: PA@HNT-like domains can limit bulk acid crystallisation and leakage
retention: chitosan plus HNT confinement should improve acid hold-up
transport_mode: tubular acid domains may support hybrid proton hopping and vehicular motion
risk_flags: interfacial dispersion quality may control continuity

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is supported as a percolated acid-interacting scaffold aiding confinement and retention.
HNTs are directly reported to host phosphoric acid in nanoconfined form and reduce leaching.
Phosphoric acid is supported as an H-bond-mediated proton-conducting phase in cold-operable composites.

instances.novelty_rationale: The pool supports chitosan with 1-D attapulgite and separately supports PA hosted in halloysite, but not chitosan with PA@HNTs. This makes the instance a plausible cross-over design focused on cold-stable confined acid transport.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous protonated phosphate glass used as a control inorganic proton conductor with intrinsically continuous transport topology.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous network directly matches continuous proton transport
retention: protonic species are strongly immobilised within the glass network
transport_mode: OH-linked relay is plausible without liquid-phase channel breakup
risk_flags: low-temperature brittleness and humidity sensitivity may limit practical membrane use
long-term conductivity stability can be conditional

element_evidence.reason: Phosphate glass is directly supported as an amorphous continuous proton conductor with strong hydrogen bonding and retained protonic species.

instances.novelty_rationale: This exact-match control is retained because it directly satisfies the continuity-focused descriptor set from the literature pool. It provides a benchmark against which softer cold-window hybrid designs can be compared.

instances.composition_description: A hybrid membrane combining protonated phosphate glass domains with a PVA continuous phase to add hydrogen-bonding flexibility around an amorphous protonic inorganic core.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: glass domains provide non-crystalline proton-transport backbone
matrix_flexibility: PVA may mitigate brittle disconnection at subzero temperatures
transport_mode: interfacial OH-rich contacts could couple inorganic and polymeric proton relay
risk_flags: phase compatibility may be difficult to optimise
conductivity may depend strongly on residual water content

element_evidence.reason: Phosphate glass is directly supported as an amorphous proton-conducting and retaining network.
PVA contributes a dense OH-mediated hydrogen-bonding landscape analogous to a flexible proton-relay interphase.

instances.novelty_rationale: The claim pool supports phosphate glass and PVA separately but does not report this hybrid. The novelty lies in pairing a phase-stable amorphous protonic inorganic with a soft OH-rich film former to better address the 182–299 K mechanical window.
